title: The Monday essay
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wood writes the essay. On a mat offcut, in the display face, one paragraph. The thesis is a sentence about frames. The instructor reads it and says it's the first thing he's turned in that's about something. He says it's about mat board. She says that's what she said.

panels.composition: A cream mat offcut. A paragraph in the display face. The strip shows the shape, not the words.

image.prompt: close on a rectangle of cream mat board with a paragraph hand-lettered on it in squared capitals, unreadable, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The INSTRUCTOR reading it at her desk. WOOD at the back. The class between them.

image.prompt: a woman instructor at her desk reading a piece of mat board while a young man waits at the back of a full classroom, black and white, no words

balloons.text: The first thing you've turned in that's about something.

image.prompt: a woman instructor looking up over a piece of mat board, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The offcut handed back. In red pen in the corner: a mark the strip draws as a smudge, and one word: 'Finally.'

image.prompt: close on a piece of mat board with a red-pen mark in its corner and one word written beneath, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: 'Finally.' The grade: a smudge.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'It's about mat board.' 'That's what I said.' The grade is a smudge; the word is Finally.
